analysis.title: Transition to a demand-driven Eurosystem
key_insights: Over the past month equities faced three simultaneous shocks: rapidly rising oil prices, spillovers from France's political and fiscal turbulence into euro area bonds, and doubts about the sustainability of AI capex. SEB sees these as noise rather than a turning point, but only if the concerns subside. Macro data and Q3 earnings remain firm.
SEB expects positive post-midterm equity performance, citing that US midterm elections have historically been followed by strong equity returns.

US economy grew well above most trend estimates in Q3, supported by firm consumer spending and AI-related investment. Core PCE inflation is rising again after the August downward revision and stays well above the 2% target, which SEB calls a dilemma for the Fed. SEB still expects consumer spending to slow as the support from unusually large tax refunds fades.

US growth is sensitive to the AI expansion and equity market performance because of its reliance on AI investment and wealthy households. SEB says the data currently support that policy is not restrictive.

The Fed held policy unchanged on 28 October with two members dissenting in favour of a 25bp hike. Chair Warsh's softer press-conference language, saying the Fed had made progress in tightening financial conditions since September, was the surprise. SEB reads this as supporting a December hike but leaving the path after that uncertain.
The Fed statement had no balance-sheet changes. Warsh has previously called for renewed balance-sheet reduction, but SEB expects any change to wait until next year.

USD bonds are range-bound. AI-stock concerns and higher energy prices drove a rotation into bonds, lowering long-end yields and flattening the curve. With forwards pricing about 70bp of hikes, SEB sees room for policy-rate expectations to soften, and expects the 10Y Treasury yield mostly near 5%.

The ECB's 29 October meeting repeated that tighter financial conditions may reduce the need for rate hikes, while stating it has tools against unwarranted market dynamics. SEB sees forwards pricing falling below 60bp of hikes in coming months, with the next hike expected in December.

The ECB is reviewing its March 2024 operational framework as the Eurosystem moves from abundant excess liquidity to a demand-driven system in which banks actively use refinancing operations. SEB expects the review in H1 2027, structural refinancing operations no earlier than late 2027, and a structural securities portfolio from 2028.
Excess liquidity is still about EUR 2.1tn and banks can source overnight funding near the deposit facility rate, so there is little incentive to borrow at the MRO rate of DFR+15bp.

The review could set out maturity, frequency, collateral and tender procedure for structural refinancing operations, priced likely off the realised MRO rate plus a spread. For the securities portfolio it could cover eligible securities, maturity guidelines and risk sharing. SEB does not expect a firm target size for the portfolio.

The ECB will introduce the new operations once it sees durable liquidity demand and the Eurosystem balance sheet starts growing durably again. Timing depends on APP and PEPP run-off pace, banks' reserve demand, take-up in existing MROs and LTROs, and money-market functioning, including a gradual firming of repo and €STR relative to the DFR.

SEB expects structural refinancing operations to come first, with maturities of one year or longer and possibly regular quarterly tranches that grow as durable reserve demand becomes clearer. Longer maturities would count toward NSFR stable funding.

The structural securities portfolio is a balance-sheet-management tool, not renewed QE or a tool to control intra-euro-area spreads. SEB thinks the ECB could temporarily resume APP and/or PEPP reinvestments if fragmentation became severe, but expects softer rhetoric and fewer hikes as the first line of defence.

Money-market implications: SEB expects €STR to rise to 1-3bp above the DFR by end-2028, and the overnight RFR Euro one-day repo rate to move from about 2.5bp above the DFR to 8-12bp above. The ECB is expected to look through temporary quarter-end repo spikes.

Swap spread view: German government bonds should initially stay rich and may richen further versus 6M Euribor swaps, because the €STR/6M Euribor basis should stay wide until liquidity stabilises and France-related turbulence eases. Later, higher repo rates and a stabilising basis should cheapen Bunds versus swaps, with the German 10Y trading flat to 6M Euribor swaps within two years.

France: the draft budget went to the National Assembly in early October. The Assembly vote is provisionally set for 17 November and the 70-day approval deadline is 17 December. With a fragmented parliament approval is uncertain. A failed budget would likely widen spreads and weigh on EUR, while approval could ease pressure. The 2027 presidential election is seen as the more decisive event.

The French-German 10Y spread has narrowed from last week's peak of 175bp to about 155bp, but renewed turbulence risk is likely to persist for months. SEB expects the German 10Y yield mostly in a 3.30-3.50% range.

EUR/USD: markets price a Democratic sweep in the 3 November midterms at about 65%. SEB expects limited lasting USD impact if the result matches expectations. A contested result could initially support USD on risk-off, but a prolonged dispute would more likely weigh on USD.

After the midterms, focus is expected to return to Middle East escalation versus de-escalation. Escalation would likely support USD through safe-haven demand and higher oil, while de-escalation would lower oil and remove a USD support. With both the Fed and ECB expected to hike in December, SEB says oil and risk sentiment matter more than rate differentials near term.

SEB's CTA proxy shows positioning close to maximum short EURUSD. Progress on the French budget or Middle East de-escalation could give EUR relief, while larger EUR downside would likely need a stronger catalyst.
earnings_insights: Q3 earnings are described as encouraging, with positive surprises continuing to dominate in the US and globally. The report gives no specific EPS or revenue figures and does not state whether the surprises are on reported or adjusted numbers.

risk_factors: Spillovers from France's political and fiscal turbulence into broader euro area bond markets, including a failed budget widening spreads and weighing on EUR.
Doubts about the sustainability of the AI capex boom, to which US growth is sensitive.
Middle East escalation after the US midterms.
A contested US midterm result, which could initially support USD on risk-off.
Fragmentation in the euro area, which could force the ECB to temporarily resume APP and/or PEPP reinvestments.
Fading support to US consumer spending from tax refunds.
vol_and_positioning: SEB's CTA proxy shows positioning close to maximum short EURUSD, so progress on the French budget or Middle East de-escalation could give EUR relief.
Forwards price about 70bp of Fed hikes and nearly 70bp of ECB hikes by autumn 2027, with SEB seeing scope for both to fall.
Betting markets price a Democratic sweep in the midterms at around 65%.
geopolitical: Reports of US briefings to Gulf allies on post-midterm military action in the Middle East, which SEB says could reflect an actual plan or positioning ahead of negotiations.
France's political and fiscal turbulence, with the draft budget in the National Assembly, a provisional 17 November vote, a 17 December approval deadline and the 2027 presidential election.
US midterm elections on 3 November, with polls and betting markets pointing to a Democratic House and narrow Democratic Senate.

tension_points.bull_case: CTA positioning is close to maximum short EURUSD, so progress on the French budget or Middle East de-escalation could give EUR relief. A prolonged contested US election result would more likely weigh on USD, and strong post-midterm equity returns would modestly support EUR.
tension_points.bear_case: A failed French budget would likely widen spreads and weigh on EUR. Middle East escalation would support USD through safe-haven demand and higher oil. A contested US result could initially support USD on risk-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A failed French budget at the 17 November Assembly vote or the 17 December approval deadline would undermine the EUR relief case.

tension_points.theme: Equity risk appetite after October shocks
tension_points.bull_case: Macro data hold up on both sides of the Atlantic, Q3 earnings surprises are positive in the US and globally, and US midterms have historically been followed by strong equity returns.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising oil prices, French fiscal spillovers into euro area bonds and doubts about AI capex sustainability have put pressure on the benign equity backdrop.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The benign view holds only if the oil, France and AI capex concerns subside. If they persist, the turbulence would be more than noise.

theme_stances.key_argument: The ECB will introduce structural refinancing operations and then a structural securities portfolio once durable liquidity demand emerges, as a balance-sheet tool and not QE.
theme_stances.evidence: Structural operations should not be confused with QE.
